question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{\sqrt{x+2}-2}{{x}^{2}-4} & =\frac{\sqrt{2+2}-2}{{2}^{2}-4}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the numerator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the numerator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{\sqrt{x+2}-2}{{x}^{2}-4} & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{\sqrt{x+2}-2}{(x-2)(x+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{(\sqrt{x+2}-2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)}{(x-2)(x+2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{{(\sqrt{x+2})}^{2}-{2}^{2}}{(x-2)(x+2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{x+2-4}{(x-2)(x+2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{x-2}{(x-2)(x+2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 2}\frac{1}{(x+2)(\sqrt{x+2}+2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(2+2)(\sqrt{2+2}+2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$
